signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry Divergence
signals.text: AUD/CHF trades at 0.5794, supported by a significant G10 bilateral divergence where AUD outperforms the G10 average by +1.496% while CHF lags by -0.677%. This 217.4bp spread represents a strong weekly theme driven by a massive +435bp OIS carry advantage for AUD (RBA AONIA 4.35% vs SNB SARON -0.07%). AUD COT LF net long is at +49,749 (pctl 94, z +1.78), indicating a crowded institutional position, while retail sentiment shows an extreme 94% short bias, creating a contrarian support layer. Price remains technically bullish, holding above the SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.7094/0.7013/0.6968 (AUD/USD basis). Trade bias: Long AUD/CHF; carry-driven outperformance persists while VIX remains at 14.5. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — hold priced. Risk: VIX clears 25, triggering a sharp unwind of the crowded carry trade and CHF safe-haven bid.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Intervention Risk + Options Skew Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY at 159.46 remains pinned near the 160.00 threshold as market headlines confirm yen weakness is back in focus for G20 officials. Despite a +268bp OIS carry advantage favoring the USD (SOFR 3.66% vs TONA 0.98%), the options market is pricing in significant downside protection with a 25d Risk Reversal of -1.81, a strong put skew. This reflects institutional hedging against potential MoF intervention rather than safe-haven demand, given the low VIX at 14.5. Speculative positioning remains heavily net short JPY (LF net -73,641, pctl 12), leaving the pair vulnerable to a squeeze if official action is taken. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, fading the carry trade near 160.00 on intervention risk. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hike bias intact. Risk: Sustained break above 160.00 without MoF action validates the carry trade and forces options-gamma covering.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs OIS Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5964 trades above its SMA200 at 0.5848, supported by a hawkish RBNZ stance heading into the September 2 meeting where 90% of economists expect a hike. However, COT data shows Leveraged Funds remain net short -27,414 (pctl 2, z -2.19), a positioning extreme that directly contradicts the OIS hike bias. RBNZ holds at 2.5%. Trade bias: Long NZD/USD; spec short-squeeze potential on RBNZ hawkishness. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — 90% hike probability. Risk: RBNZ holds rates steady, validating the spec short and collapsing the hike-premium.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Vol Premium + Real Rate Support
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3590, supported by a mildly restrictive real policy rate of +0.85%, which ranks among the highest in the G10. The options market shows an elevated Vol Risk Premium (VRP) of +6.2%, with 1M IV at 11.0% vs HV30 at 4.8%, signaling that traders are paying a high premium for protection despite price holding above the SMA20/50 cluster at 1.3537/1.3418. COT positioning is at a 92nd percentile long (+46,070), suggesting a crowded trend, but moderate ESI data (-9.3) indicates that growth surprises are not currently driving the bid. Trade bias: Neutral/Bullish GBP/USD; supported by real rates but capped by vol-hedging and positioning. Catalyst: Fed Chair Warsh at Jackson Hole. Risk: US 10Y yield surges, closing the 38bp UK-US 10Y spread and triggering a GBP long-unwind.
